description:
## Outcome

After the local release and GitHub publication work is complete, `mikehostetler/homebrew-tap` contains a `jido-cli` formula that installs the accepted macOS ARM64 archive and tests `jido --version`.

## Work

1. Use the immutable GitHub release URL and exact SHA-256 value from the accepted artifact.
2. Install the packaged `bin/jido` without a Homebrew Erlang or Elixir dependency.
3. Add non-interactive formula tests for version and basic help.
4. Add update automation that changes version, URL, and checksum in a reviewable pull request.
5. Document install, upgrade, uninstall, and artifact support.
6. Add other target selectors only after those artifacts pass their native release flow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `brew install mikehostetler/tap/jido-cli` selects the accepted artifact.
- [ ] `brew deps jido-cli` does not add Erlang or Elixir.
- [ ] A bad checksum fails installation.
- [ ] The formula has no service definition.
- [ ] Update automation does not push directly to the tap default branch.

## Tests

Run formula audit, install, help, version, bad-checksum, and upgrade tests.

## Non-goals

Do not start this task before the local release and GitHub artifact exist. Do not add a daemon, service, or `homebrew/core` submission.
title: Publish Jido through the Homebrew tap
